text: Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture at St.
James' Park, as Newcastle United host Arsenal.
After a sluggish start to the season, seventh-placed Newcastle are unbeaten in their last six games, winning four of these.
Held to a 2-2 draw by Wolves last time out, the Magpies will still come into this game high on confidence, after a massive 3-0 away win over Manchester United in their midweek Carabao Cup tie.
Third-placed Arsenal are yet to lose a game in this Premier League season so far, and a victory by five or more goals, however unlikely, would send them top of the table.
The Gunners dispatched bottom side Sheffield United 5-0 in their last home game, but did suffer a 3-1 defeat to West Ham in the Carabao Cup prior to this one.

Despite several fringe players making huge impressions against Manchester United in midweek, Eddie Howe keeps faith with the side that started Newcastle’s 2-2 draw with Wolves in their last league game.
Callum Wilson’s first-half brace got the Magpies off to a strong start in the West Midlands, and he’ll be looking to do the same here, flanked by Anthony Gordon and Miguel Almiron.
Arsenal, meanwhile, make six changes from their 3-1 League Cup loss, with only Ben White, Gabriel, Jorginho, Kai Havertz and Eddie Nketiah keeping their places.
The latter scored a superb hat-trick against Sheffield United at the Emirates, and will no doubt be keen to get his name on the scoresheet at least once more at St.
James’.
The teams are lined up on the pitch, and we'll be ready for kick-off straight after the playing of the Last Post to honour those fallen in conflicts throughout the world.
KICK-OFF: Nketiah gets the game underway for Arsenal, who will look to get on the front foot right from the off!
Newcastle have won just one of their last 10 Premier League games against Arsenal, losing eight, drawing once and failing to score on eight occasions during that run.
Nketiah makes a darting run into the box as Martinelli whips in a cross, but Schar's there to nod the ball away for the Magpies.
Almiron and Wilson look to combine as Newcastle launch a counter-attack, but the latter is clipped late by Gabriel to win the hosts a free-kick.
A first-time cross off Guimaraes' cut-back is curled into the box by Longstaff, but Raya gets off his line well for Arsenal to punch the ball well clear.
Only Manchester United (14) have won more Premier League away games at St.
James' Park than Arsenal (13), with the Gunners winning eight of their last 10 visits to Newcastle in the top-flight.
An injury to Joelinton sees the Brazilian head to the sideline temporarily, but he's up and ready to continue for over 30 seconds until finally being allowed back onto the pitch by the referee!
Saka defies his size to shrug Burn off the ball with little difficulty, but he doesn't get far before being shunted over the sideline himself by Joelinton!
Guimaraes is crowded out on the edge of his own box and the ball breaks for Tomiyasu, but his first-time shot goalwards is deflected behind off Burn for a corner!
Jorginho tees up Martinelli on the edge of the box, but his curling strike from 25 yards is an easy one for Lascelles to get in the way of.
Intense pressure from Almiron forces Gabriel back and into a rushed, deflected clearance, but a shove from the Paraguayan results in a free-kick to let Arsenal off the hook!
A deflected Saka shot is played wide by Rice to Martinelli, but England winger hesitates from striking the deflected cross back towards goal!
Saliba sizes up a shot and has a go from range, but Lascelles jumps out of the defensive line to make the block and send the ball looping behind for another Arsenal corner!
Saka's delivery from the corner is punched half-clear by Pope, but Jorginho's follow-up on the volley is sent sailing well over the top!
Rice advances up the left and wins another corner which is played short to Martinelli.
His cross to the far post is attacked by Nketiah, but the striker can't get enough on his header to send the ball on-target.
Newcastle are unbeaten in their last six league games, scoring at least twice in each of the last five.
They last scored 2+ goals in six consecutive Premier League games between August and October 2004.
Jorginho scoops the ball over the top of the defence for Tomiyasu to chase, but he can't latch onto the pass ahead of Trippier and it'll go behind for a goal-kick.
OVER!!! The first clear-cut chance of the match, but it's wasted by Newcastle! From Guimaraes' high ball to the back post, Burn's header back across goal is deflected into the path of Wilson.
He looks to volley goalwards with Raya in no-man's land, but fires it straight over the bar from close range as the offside flag is raised!
Burn catches Saka very late indeed, and is very, very lucky to avoid a yellow card there after committing an earlier foul against the same player!
Trippier looks to pick out the run of Guimaraes into the box with a scooped pass over the top, but Nketiah is back there for Arsenal and heads the ball away!
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 Premier League games, winning eight scoring 28 goals.
All three of their draws have been 2-2 scorelines in London derbies over the course of this run.

Havertz absolutely flies in on Longstaff with a wild, unnecessary challenge, sparking a large-scale fracas between both sets of players and being shown a card which he's very fortunate is yellow rather than red!
Gordon's reaction to Havertz's challenge saw both teams pile into the melee, and the Newcastle winger is also shown a yellow card by the referee.
Longstaff was on the receiving end of that wild Havertz challenge, but his appeals to the referee also earn him a yellow card!

Schar's comments to the official are also received with distaste and a yellow card goes the way of the Newcastle defender, and a perplexing last few minutes certainly won't have earned referee Stuart Atwell many friends in Newcastle!
CHANCE!!! Trippier overlaps to latch onto Almiron's back-heel and whip in a cross.
Wilson's glancing header is skewed out to Gordon, who can't get a shot away in time as Raya dives onto the loose ball!
Trippier is making his 150th Premier League starting appearance, 54 of which have been with Newcastle, 58 with Tottenham and 38 with Burnley.
Havertz's throughball almost puts Nketiah through on goal, but he's muscled off the ball by Lascelles in a legal and fair challenge!
Guimaraes finds a pocket of space on the edge of the box and lets fly, but drags his 20-yard shot a few yards wide of the target!
We'll play four additional minutes to close out a cagey first-half at St.
James, and you get the feeling that a goal at either end could blow this game wide open!
SAVED!!! Martinelli skips past Trippier as he cuts inside off the left, but with options queuing up in the box the winger chooses to shoot and fires a tame shot straight into the gloves of Pope!
A late, and by the looks of it blatant, elbow to the back of Jorginho's head by Guimaraes has been missed by the referee, and VAR haven't intervened either.
You can't help but feel that if the officials had seen that in real time, the Newcastle midfielder's match might be over...
Almiron and Trippier combine once more and the latter's cross leaves Raya stranded, but Saliba rises high to knock the ball away with a commanding defensive header!
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 0-0 ARSENAL.

Goalless at the break, as a first-half sparse with chances but high on drama comes to an end! Neither goalkeeper has really been tested, with Raya diffusing a close-range effort from Gordon and Martinelli shooting straight into the gloves of Pope.
However, the cards began to flow with half-time approaching, particularly after a reckless lunge from Havertz.

He was lucky to only pick up a yellow card, but the reactions of Gordon, Longstaff and Schar also earned the three Newcastle players bookings, while Guimaraes was lucky to avoid a sanction for a late elbow on Jorginho! It's not boiled over - yet - but a goal early in the second period could certainly see this edgy, tight match in the north east take an entirely different complexion.
On the front foot for much of that first half, Arsenal were still stunted in the final third by well-organised Newcastle defence.

Nketiah had four touches in the box and contested nine duels but could only manage one off-target shot, while Martinelli created three chances and had the only effort on target in the opening 45 minutes.
Let's hope the game opens up somewhat in the second half, and both sides' attackers come to the fore!
Burn comes off for the Magpies in the only half-time change to be made, and Tino Livramento's introduction will see Trippier shift from right-back to the left.
KICK-OFF: Longstaff resumes proceedings at St.
James', kicking off the second period for the hosts in black and white!
Arsenal counter as Rice opens up space for Martinelli.
He looks to beat Livramento around the outside, but the Newcastle substitute gets across well to shield the ball and prevents giving Arsenal a corner!
White hangs up a cross from the byline with Rice arriving late at the back post, but the midfielder can't get a clean connection on his header and Pope collects the ball with ease!

Newcastle are the first side to see three players booked for dissent and/or arguments in the first half of a Premier League game since then-champions Leicester City against Stoke City in December 2016.
Gordon is sent running in behind thanks to a fantastic Guimaraes throughball, but he refrains from shooting after cutting inside, and a poor pass back to Guimaraes sees Newcastle lose possession!
CHANCE!!! Newcastle break away at speed after Nketiah fails to get a shot away in their box.

Great hold-up play from Wilson allows Almiron to latch onto the ball and surge through the middle before linking up with Gordon, but the winger again delays his shot and White makes a timely block! It's just not coming off in the final third at the moment for Newcastle!
A mis-kicked volley from Martinelli falls kindly for Havertz, but his shot from the edge of the area takes a deflection off Nketiah and Pope is able to collect.

Newcastle are unbeaten in all 17 of their Premier League home games when they've been level at half-time under Eddie Howe's tutelage, winning nine, drawing eight, and keeping a clean sheet in nine of their last 11 such matches.
An hour gone and still no goals, but there's certainly been no let-up in the intensity or the feeling going into some of these challenges.
Guimaraes and Jorginho's continuing battle is certainly one to keep an eye on, while you get the feeling Havertz could be walking a tightrope too!
WIDE!!! Martinelli finds space to cross from the left and hangs the ball up towards the back post.
Trippier nods it half-clear, but Rice follows in with a bullet header that whistles just wide of Pope's right-hand upright!
Newcastle make their next alterations of the second half, with Wilson withdrawn for Joe Willock in a change that will likely see Gordon move into the centre of their attack.
Almiron also comes off for the Magpies, but his replacement is very much like-for-like in the form of Jacob Murphy.
WIDE!!! Joelinton sets off on a barnstorming run forward, but loses possession on the edge of the box.
Arsenal can't clear properly though and the ball falls to Murphy, who drills a low ball across the face of goal and wide!
GOOOOOOAAAAAALLL!!!! St.
James' Park ERUPTS!!! Willock keeps Murphy's prior effort in play and crosses back into the middle, where Joelinton contests Raya for the ball.

It ricochets on the goal-line, but Gordon's there to tap into an empty net and put the Magpies 1-0 up! The referee's had a word in his ear though, and we may not quite have heard the last of this one yet...

Joelinton undoubtedly rose and headed with the intention of scoring himself, but it instead bounced kindly to tee Gordon up for the simplest of finishes, which looks like it's put Newcastle 1-0 up here!

We're yet to restart as the VAR officials are checking almost every element of that passage of play, with questions over whether Willock kept the ball in play, Joelinton fouled Raya, and if Gordon was offside or not!
GOAL GIVEN!!! All three queries are cleared by VAR with insufficient evidence to overturn any of them, and Newcastle's fans get another chance to celebrate as their 1-0 lead is set in stone!

Anthony Gordon has now scored four goals in three successive Premier League seasons - 2021-22 and 2022-23 also - and after a slow start to his Magpies career, Gordon is now an integral part of this Newcastle side!
The onus is now on Arsenal to respond with a goal of their own, but coming up against the side with the second-best goal difference in the division, that won't be an easy task by any means!
Martinelli fires an Arsenal corner in towards the near post, but Murphy's flick sends the ball up, over and behind for another set-piece.
White comes off in Arsenal's first change of the match, with Tomiyasu shifting to right-back and Oleksandr Zinchenko entering the fray.
Newcastle have now scored in their last nine Premier League games, the last six in a row at home, and are unbeaten in their last five after going 1-0 up.
Arsenal have had a huge 89.2 per cent possession over the last 15 minutes, but have conceded to find themselves 1-0 down during that time!
Murphy pulls away from a challenge with Zinchenko with what looks like a pulled or dislocated shoulder, and there's no way he'll be able to carry on without getting that issue seen to quickly.
Last week's hat-trick hero Nketiah's hardly had a sniff this time around, and comes off now for Leandro Trossard in a change that could see Martinelli move into a central role.
Jorginho is also brought off late by Mikel Arteta, with Fabio Vieira on for the remainder of this unbelievably tight contest.
Murphy is sadly forced off just 16 minutes after coming on, and Matt Ritchie will replace the wideman for the last 10 or so minutes.
Nketiah is Arsenal’s highest scorer in the Premier League this season, with five goals from just seven shots on target.
However, just one of his 19 goals overall in the competition has come north of London (v Burnley in May 2019), with all five strikes this season coming at the Emirates.
Ritchie and Gordon combine down the right as the latter sends a cross straight into the gloves of Raya, but the offside flag's up to give Arsenal a free-kick regardless.

As well as being the joint-highest goalscorers in the Premier League this season with 26 goals, Newcastle had the best shot conversion rate (18.6 per cent) and the second-highest expected goals total (22.1) in the competition prior to this game.
Their singular goal from just two shots on target in this game suggest that this trend is set to continue for some time!
BLOCKED!!! A corner is played short and the ball eventually comes to Trossard on the edge of the box, but his right-footed effort is blocked by a double effort from Livramento and Lascelles!
Guimaraes shoves Vieira off the ball with a push to the face of the Arsenal midfielder, and is finally shown the yellow card he arguably should've picked up in the first half.
EIGHT additional minutes to play on the Tyne, and after the drama and fine margins we've already seen here, get ready for plenty more before the full-time whistle comes!
A wayward Livramento challenge makes contract with both the ball and Martinelli, taking the Arsenal winger down on the touchline and receiving a yellow card from the man in the middle.

A smart flick forward from Joelinton sends Gordon racing away down the right, but Arsenal are able to get back in numbers to prevent a cross, before the offside flag is raised for the goalscorer anyway!

Trossard's blocked effort just minutes ago was the only shot on target Arsenal have managed in the entire second half, and with stats like that it's no wonder they haven't been able to find a way back into this game!
Martinelli tees up Zinchenko to cross from the byline, but the substitute's drilled cut-back is intercepted and thumped clear by Lascelles.
It's a real backs-to-the-wall job for Newcastle now!
After a free-kick is punched half-clear by Pope, Arsenal keep on coming back at Newcastle through Zinchenko.
He tees up Trossard, but the Belgian's first-time shot takes a huge deflection and skews behind for a corner!
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 1-0 ARSENAL.

It's all over, and Newcastle hold out by the barest of margins to sneak to a 1-0 victory over Arsenal! A close-run, scrappy game was settled by an even scrappier goal, with Gordon's close-range tap-in requiring a five-minute VAR check before being given the green light.

After both he and Murphy fluffed chances to score either side of Rice heading wide for Arsenal, Gordon's 63rd minute tap-in was a just reward for Newcastle, who improved significantly from a flat first-half performance.

Arsenal piled on the pressure as they chased an equaliser, but couldn't test Pope in any meaningful way as the Magpies' defence held firm to condemn the Gunners to a first Premier League defeat of the season.
Three points in a game that was far from black and white take Newcastle up two places into sixth, while Arsenal remain third having missed the chance to potentially go top of the table.
They fail to close the gap on the top two, with arch-rivals Tottenham now the only side yet to lose a game in this season's top-flight.
